title: 心理学 Day 25：死亡心理学 — 向死而生的科学
title_en: Psychology Day 25: The Psychology of Death — The Science of Living Toward Death

questions.question: 按 Carstensen 的社会情绪选择理论，一个 25 岁的人得知自己下个月要移居远方，他的社交选择最可能怎样变化？为什么？
options: 更积极地结识新朋友、拓展人脉，因为年轻人的动机始终以获取新信息和向外扩展为主导
更倾向于独处，因为意识到分离会让人回避所有关系以减少离别的痛苦
基本不变，因为只有真正进入老年后，人的社交偏好才会转向深度关系
更偏向少数亲密的人，因为决定动机转向的是感知到的时间视野，而不是实际年龄
questions.explanation: 文章说关键变量是感知到的时间视野而不是年龄：只要让年轻人想象即将搬去远方，他们的选择就会像老年人一样偏向亲密的人。认为「只有老了才会转向」，正是把年龄误当成了原因。
questions.question_en: Under Carstensen's socioemotional selectivity theory, how is a 25-year-old who learns they'll move far away next month most likely to change their social choices, and why?
options_en: They'll seek out new friends and contacts more actively, because young people's motivation is always dominated by new information and outward expansion
They'll withdraw into solitude, because awareness of separation makes people avoid all relationships to spare the pain of goodbyes
Little will change, because social preferences shift toward deep ties only once people actually reach old age
They'll favor a few close people, because what shifts motivation is the perceived time horizon, not chronological age
questions.explanation_en: The piece says the key variable is perceived time horizon, not age: simply having young people imagine an impending move makes their choices resemble older adults', favoring intimates. Assuming the shift comes only with old age mistakes age for the cause.

questions.question: 一位丧亲的朋友说，自己有时能笑出来、专心处理工作，担心这说明自己「没走完哀伤的阶段」「在逃避」。按文中更有证据的模型，该怎么看？
options: 这是正常的：健康的哀伤在面向丧失与面向重建之间来回摆荡
这是逃避的信号：哀伤必须依次经过否认、愤怒、讨价还价、抑郁才能到达接受
这需要尽快寻求专业干预，因为能正常生活说明情绪被压抑，日后会更严重
这说明哀伤已经结束，之后不应再出现悲伤和思念，否则就是复发
questions.explanation: Stroebe 与 Schut 的双过程模型认为，健康的哀伤在悲伤思念与处理生活之间摆荡；「五阶段」是被误用的神话，Kübler-Ross 描述的是临终者，且没有证据表明哀伤按固定顺序走。Bonanno 还发现韧性是最常见的反应，多数人不需要正式干预。
questions.question_en: A bereaved friend says they sometimes laugh and can focus on work, and worries this means they "haven't finished the stages of grief" and are "in avoidance." By the better-supported model in the piece, how should this be seen?
options_en: It's normal: healthy grief oscillates between loss-oriented and restoration-oriented states
It's a sign of avoidance: grief must pass through denial, anger, bargaining and depression in order before reaching acceptance
It calls for prompt professional help, since functioning normally means emotions are being suppressed and will worsen later
It means grieving is over, so any later sadness or longing would count as a relapse
questions.explanation_en: Stroebe and Schut's dual process model holds that healthy grief swings between sorrow and getting on with life. The five stages are a misapplied myth—Kübler-Ross described the dying, not the bereaved, and there's no evidence grief follows a fixed order. Bonanno also found resilience is the most common response; most people need no formal intervention.

questions.question: 有人读了「向死而生」，决定「假装明天就会死，所以今天拼命工作、多出成果」。按文中的判别标准，这更像什么？
options: 正是念死修行的目标：通过持续高强度的努力松动「我执」
更像死亡焦虑的缓冲在运作：把有限性塞回了靠成就撑起的自尊防御，而不是真正的死亡觉知
正是向死而生的本义：觉知有限后提高产出，说明注意力被成功校准到了当下
正是社会情绪选择理论预测的转向：时间有限时，人会转向追求未来回报
questions.explanation: 文中说「假装明天就死所以今天拼命卷」是对死亡觉察的扭曲，它回到了恐惧管理理论里的自尊防御。判别标准是：死亡觉察若让你更焦虑地追逐，多半是缓冲在运作；若让你更松、更敢拒绝、更在场，才是觉知在起效。时间有限时人恰恰会从未来回报转向情感意义。
questions.question_en: After reading about "being-toward-death," someone resolves to "live as if I'll die tomorrow, so work flat out and produce more today." By the article's test, what does this most resemble?
options_en: The goal of maraṇasati practice: loosening attachment to self through sustained intense effort
A death-anxiety buffer at work: it stuffs finitude back into achievement-based self-esteem defense rather than genuine awareness of death
The true meaning of being-toward-death: awareness of finitude raises output, showing attention has been recalibrated to the present
Exactly the shift socioemotional selectivity predicts: when time is short, people turn toward future payoffs
questions.explanation_en: The piece calls "act as if you'll die tomorrow and grind harder today" a distortion that slips back into the self-esteem buffer of terror management theory. Its test: if death awareness makes you chase more anxiously, a buffer is probably operating; if it makes you looser, readier to say no, more present, awareness is working. When time feels short, people actually shift from future payoffs to emotional meaning.
